meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (1MA1/3F, Monday 11 November 2024, P75161A). Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: Coded WITH mark_split. Every (Total for Question) line was recovered except q1–q5, each of which is a single mark; the paper sums to the printed 80.

coding_notes: q1 (value of a digit in a whole number) tagged decimals, the documented handling for place value — and the same node EDEXCEL-JUN25-F-P3 q1 uses for a digit after the decimal point.
q5 (square root of a terminating decimal) tagged indices, the documented handling for roots.

q11a and q11b tagged converting_measurements. There is no node for reading a conversion graph and no precedent row in the audit; the graph is the given conversion factor and the question is a unit conversion, so this is 'inside an existing skill's territory' rather than a taxonomy gap.

q14 tagged simple_arithmetic alone. An hourly rate with a 1½-times weekend multiplier could carry proportion as well, but every mark in the scheme is a multiplication or an addition of money and adding a Ratio-topic skill would move four marks out of Number for no gain in what the row claims.

q21 (percentage profit on a ratio-split stock) tagged ratio BEFORE percentage_change. Two of the five marks are the ratio split and only the last is the percentage, and the mark scheme's first process mark is 240 ÷ (3 + 5) — the same 'lead with the skill the first mark rewards' reasoning used for q11 and for EDEXCEL-NOV24-F-P1 q22a. It also matters here: this paper is the audit's worst case for Number over-representation (see the note on the topic column below) and percentage_change is filed under Number.

THIS PAPER IS 50% NUMBER, against Edexcel's published 22-28% Foundation weighting — the most extreme instance in the audit of the documented topic-straddle and classification problem, worse than the 1F June 2025 case the coding doc describes at 38%. Four causes, none of them a tagging error: time_calculations (5 marks of timetables) and converting_measurements (4 marks of a conversion graph) are filed under Number; the index skills (3 marks) are too; and fractions_of_amounts leads q9, a 5-mark question that is really about percentages of two subgroups. Do not read this paper's topic percentages. The fix the coding doc names — splitting an item's marks across its skills' topics — would help here more than anywhere else in the corpus.

q22 (compare two distributions from a stem and leaf diagram against a stated median and range) tagged median then range — the two statistics the four marks are split between, two for identifying School A's and two for the comparisons.
q25b ((m²)⁻³) tagged simplifying_indices rather than fractional_and_negative_indices: the operation is a power of a power, and simplifying_indices is the lower node that honestly covers it.
